transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I just feel worn down almost all the time. Even if I sleep through the night, I don’t really feel rested. By the time I get through work and deal with the clutter at home, I feel like I have almost nothing left for anything else.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, even activities you used to like?

Yeah, I think so. Most days there’s kind of this low, gray mood in the background. I can still go to the lab and talk to people and do what I need to do, but I don’t feel light or excited about things the way I used to. Even stuff like baking or checking the telescope just doesn’t really feel the same.
Do you feel fatigued or experience a lack of energy most days, even after resting?
Yes. I feel worn down most of the time, even if I’ve slept through the night. After I get through work and deal with stuff around the house, I usually feel like I don’t have much left.
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or like you’re not worth much lately?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think of it as feeling worthless, exactly. I get frustrated with myself sometimes, but I haven’t noticed a lot of guilt or anything like that.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes. Most days I feel kind of down, like there’s this low, gray mood in the background. I can still get through work and talk to people, but I don’t really feel light or excited about things the way I used to.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that you can't sit still and feel restless?
I haven’t really noticed that. I don’t think I’m moving unusually slow, and I don’t feel like I can’t sit still.
Have you had any thoughts about not wanting to live or felt like you’d be better off dead?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t had thoughts about wanting to die or being better off dead.
Have you had trouble concentrating on tasks, even things you used to find straightforward?

Yes, I have noticed that. Things that used to feel pretty straightforward, like revising a paragraph for a grant or deciding what materials to use for a home repair, take me longer now. My mind just feels slower, and I end up second-guessing small decisions more than I used to.
How long have you been feeling this way with the low mood and fatigue?
It’s been a little over two years, I think. It started not long after we moved into the older house, and since then my mood and energy have just kind of stayed at this lower baseline.
Can you recall if there’s anything you used to do that you don’t do anymore because it just doesn’t interest you or feel enjoyable, even a little?

Yeah. I still do things, like go to the lab and talk to people, but there’s this low, gray mood most days that makes it hard to feel interested or excited. I used to enjoy baking more, and I’d get a little thrill out of checking the telescope, but now those things just feel kind of flat.

Can you tell me more about how you feel when you engage in activities like baking or checking the telescope now compared to before—do you feel no interest at all, less interest, or some interest but not the same as before?

It’s not no interest at all. I can still do them, and sometimes I’ll get into it a little. But it’s definitely less than before. Most days there’s this low, gray feeling in the background, so baking or checking the telescope just doesn’t feel as light or exciting as it used to.
Can you say that there are still some activities you enjoy a little, or has it gotten to the point where almost nothing feels pleasurable anymore?

There are still some things I enjoy a little. It’s not like nothing feels good at all. I can still go to the lab, talk to people, bake sometimes, check the telescope… but most days there’s this low, gray mood in the background, and those things just don’t feel as enjoyable or exciting as they used to.
Can you say that the enjoyment you get from activities is noticeably less than it used to be, even for most of them?

Yes, it’s noticeably less. I can still do most things, like go to the lab or talk to people, but there’s this low, gray feeling most days. Things like baking or checking the telescope just don’t feel light or exciting the way they used to.
Have there been times when you lost interest or pleasure in almost everything, including activities you used to enjoy the most?
I don’t think it’s gotten to almost everything, no. It’s more that things feel dulled down. I still get some interest or enjoyment here and there, just not as much as before.
Have you experienced a time when you completely lost interest or pleasure in most activities, even ones you used to really enjoy?
Not completely, no. I’ve had times where things felt pretty flat or less worth doing, but I can’t say I lost interest in most activities altogether. It’s more muted than gone.
Have you noticed that you take much less pleasure or interest in activities you used to enjoy, even if you still do them?

Yes. I still do those things, but there’s a lot less pleasure in them. Most days it’s like this low gray mood is just sitting in the background, and things like baking or checking the telescope don’t feel light or exciting like they used to.
Have you had days where even the things you used to enjoy the most felt so flat or uninteresting that you barely wanted to do them, even if you still did them?

Yes, there have been days like that. I’ll still go to the lab and talk to people and get through things, but there’s this low, gray mood in the background. Even stuff I usually like, like baking or checking the telescope, just doesn’t feel light or exciting the way it used to.
Have you noticed that, even when you do activities you used to enjoy, like baking or checking the telescope, you feel very little pleasure or interest in them most of the time?

Yes, most of the time it’s more like… I’m doing the activity, but I’m not getting much from it. There’s just this low, gray mood in the background. I can still go to the lab, talk to people, bake, check the telescope, but I don’t really feel light or excited about it like I used to.
Can you say that your low mood has been present most of the day, nearly every day, for the entire time you've been feeling this way?

Yes, I’d say it’s there most days. It’s not always intense, but it’s kind of running in the background through the day. I can still go to the lab and talk to people, but I don’t feel light or excited about things the way I used to.
